title: Stand a fallen bottle back up on a moving conveyor before it reaches the guide
instruction: One bottle has fallen over on the conveyor. Stand it back up, cap up, on its own carrier before it reaches the guide rails, and let go of it, without disturbing the upright bottles.
context: On bottling, filling and labelling lines a bottle that falls over jams the guide or star wheel at the next machine and stops the line; operators stand fallen bottles back up on the moving line rather than pulling them off and losing them from the batch. It needs a pick from a carrier that doesn't stop, a quarter turn in the hand, and a centred placement back on the same moving carrier. Done by: production line operators and packing-line workers.
setup: Positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart on an oak table, 110 x 130 cm): x forward, y to the robot's left. A conveyor line runs across the table parallel to the line through the arm bases, its centre 32 cm in front of it: a black track bed (10 cm wide, 128 cm long, 1.5 cm tall, centred, ending 1 cm inside each table edge) with three grey aluminium carrier plates (10 x 10 x 1.5 cm) riding 2 mm above it, square to it, their centres starting 13 cm to the right, 11 cm to the left and 35 cm to the left of the midpoint. Each carrier holds one bottle: a white HDPE cylinder 6 cm across and 13 cm tall, filled and capped (350 g), its top 1.5 cm red (the cap). The bottles on the first two carriers (from the right) stand upright in the carrier's middle. The bottle on the third carrier lies on its side in the carrier's middle, its axis along the line, cap pointing right (downstream). The guide: two steel rails (1 cm thick, 32 cm long, 6 cm tall) along the line from 18 cm to 50 cm right of the midpoint, their inner faces 9 cm apart and centred on the line, their undersides 6.25 cm above the table (3 cm above the carriers' tops), each held from outside by two 1.2 cm square steel posts standing on the table 1 cm out from the bed's edge, 21 cm and 47 cm right of the midpoint, with a flat bracket from each post's top to the rail. Two strips of red tape (6 x 1.2 cm) mark the guide's mouth across the table on both sides of the bed, 18 cm right of the midpoint, 3 cm out from the bed. Nothing else is on the table. The line starts with the trial: the carriers speed up from rest to 2 cm/s toward the robot's right in 0.5 s and run on at that speed, so the fallen bottle's carrier reaches the guide's mouth 26.75 s into the trial. Past the table's right edge the line turns down and drops the carriers and anything on them out of reach.
scoring: Decided when the fallen bottle's carrier (its centre) reaches the guide's mouth (the red tape), from the fallen bottle's state then. 1.0 if it stands upright (axis within 10 degrees of vertical, cap up) on its own carrier, underside within 1 cm of the carrier's top, centre within 1.5 cm of the carrier's centre across the line and 2.5 cm along it, moving with the carrier (relative speed under 5 cm/s), and let go (both grippers' grasp points, between the fingers, 8 cm or more from its centre). 0.5 if it stands upright on its own carrier (centre over the carrier's top face) but is still held or not centred, or stands upright, let go, on the table off the line. 0.25 if it is off the line but not upright: no part of it over the track bed, or its lowest point 2 cm or more above the carriers' tops (held up), and it is not off the table. 0 otherwise (still lying on its carrier or the bed, standing on the bed between carriers, or off the table). Then minus 0.5 for each upright bottle disturbed, not below 0: an upright bottle is disturbed if, at any time before its own carrier reaches the guide's mouth, it tilts more than 20 degrees, its centre moves more than 3 cm (horizontally) from its carrier's centre, or its underside rises more than 2 cm above its carrier's top.
reset_notes: Stop the line, put the carriers back at their starting positions, stand the two upright bottles in the middle of the first two carriers and lay the third bottle on its side in the middle of the third, cap pointing right; start the line with the trial. Catch bottles that run off the end of the line.
fidelity: The carriers follow their path exactly, like a stiff servo-driven pallet conveyor: the arms can't push or stop them. They float 2 mm above the bed and past the table's edge move straight down. The bottles are rigid plain cylinders (no neck or shoulder; the cap is painted on) with rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The fallen bottle lies along the line, so the line's gentle start (under 0.1 m/s²) can't roll it. The jam isn't simulated: the score is decided at the guide's mouth.
